text:
maria: Acme POC — streaming from TS SDK over wss is intermittently stalling when routed through their corporate proxy. They get a few chunks then client shows no more messages, connection stays open.
katie: Repro steps? SDK version? Proxy type?
maria: Using @redwood/sdk v0.9.2 (TS), WebSocketTransport. Customer proxy is an outbound corporate appliance doing TLS inspection + HTTP/1.1 chunked proxying. They see 200 + Transfer-Encoding: chunked then no more frames.
aj: Can you paste client logs? any WS frames received after stall?
maria: Logger snippet from client:
```
INFO websocket connected
DEBUG recv chunk size=1024
DEBUG recv chunk size=2048
DEBUG recv chunk size=0  <-- then nothing
ERROR streaming stalled: read timeout
```
sam: Sounds like backpressure from proxy chunk coalescing or gzip interfering. Some proxies buffer until a threshold then flush, breaks streaming semantics.
frank: Also check if proxy is rewriting content-length or adding `Connection: close` semantics. We had a similar case where the proxy converted `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` to buffered response.
katie: Customer says they can't change proxy rules. Any SDK client-side workaround?
aj: Two options: 1) fallback to polling/long-poll non-stream mode (disable streaming in SDK) 2) switch transport to TLS tunnel (CONNECT) so proxy does not inspect chunks (use wss over 443 via proxy tunnel).
maria: They tried toggling streaming false — works but kills low-latency UX.
sam: Another workaround: add a small keepalive chunk every X seconds from server side to keep proxy flushing. But cannot guarantee modifying server behavior for POC.
frank: Can the TS SDK set `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate` off or force `no-transform` header? Some proxies respect `no-transform` and avoid buffering.
aj: Code snippet they used:
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  transport: new WebSocketTransport({ url: 'wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` } }),
  streaming: true
});
```
katie: Try using `env NO_PROXY` for the host to bypass proxy for testing, or set `proxy: 'tunnel'` in their node agent so it uses CONNECT (tunneling) instead of http proxying.

maria: Customer can't bypass corporate proxy globally but can allow list outbound host via proxy rules. Asking for a reproducible test we can give ops.
ci-bot: deploy:staging succeeded for streaming-service @ 1745600450
sam: For immediate triage: ask them to run a curl test to show chunked flush behavior via proxy:
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://demo.redwood.ai/chunk-test
```
If curl streams through their proxy it's a server/proxy issue; if curl also stalls then proxy is buffering.

maria: They ran curl -N and saw the same stalling. Ops team says proxy is buffering up to 64KB and then flushing.
frank: Ok that confirms proxy behavior. Suggest two customer options: 1) allowlist tunnel for wss host 2) use non-streaming fallback during POC 3) we can implement a server-side heartbeat chunk as temporary.
katie: I'll propose: (A) temporary server heartbeat + SDK patch to expose `transportOptions.tunnel` toggle so they can try tunneling client-side. Also quote impact to UX if streaming disabled.
aj: I'll open an internal ticket to add `transportOptions.tunnel` flag to TS SDK and document the `NO_PROXY` / proxy-tunnel guidance. PR ETA: 48h.
maria: I'll convey options to customer and request allowlist for wss host in proxy so we can test tunneling.
sam: If they accept allowlist, we should run an end-to-end capture and confirm behavior. If not, we'll enable heartbeat chunk for POC only.
maria: Thanks team. Scheduling 30m call with customer for 20:00 PST to test allowlist. @katie @aj please join.
katie: will do :thumbsup:
aj: adding to calendar.
frank: letting infra know about potential temporary heartbeat.
maria: leaving notes here for handoff after call.
